title: Glioblastoma Multiforme
summary:
TCGA glioblastoma is the cohort on which most glioma computational biology was built, and 1,753 articles reference it in methods or results. Its imaging is its least-used asset: radiology exists for 607 of 617 cases and histopathology for 389, held in the Imaging Data Commons rather than the GDC, which is why most analyses treat it as a molecular-only cohort.
Its follow-up is the fact most likely to trip up a new user. Median recorded follow-up is 12.0 months across 596 of 617 cases, reaching 127 months at the maximum - shorter than many users expect, because it reflects last recorded contact rather than total observation.
one_liner: 617 glioblastomas with twelve measurement types including radiology on 607 and pathology slides on 389 - the reference glioma cohort, with a median follow-up of 12.0 months.

useful_for.question: Do imaging features add prognostic or subtype information beyond molecular data in glioblastoma?
useful_for.rationale: Radiology on 607 cases and pathology slides on 389, paired with expression on 293, methylation on 423 and copy number on 599 for the same patients. Glioma is the disease where imaging is most clinically central, and this pairing is openly available.
useful_for.statistical_note: The intersection of imaging and expression is well below 617; build it explicitly. Imaging is in a separate repository from the molecular data.

useful_for.question: Does a new glioma classifier reproduce established methylation subgroups?
useful_for.rationale: Methylation on 423 cases with subgroup definitions established across a large literature makes this the standard validation set for glioma classification.
useful_for.statistical_note: Extensive prior use means good performance here is weak evidence of generalization.

useful_for.question: Which molecular features associate with survival in glioblastoma?
useful_for.rationale: Vital status is informative for 96.3% of 617 cases, giving a clean overall survival endpoint on a well-characterized cohort.
useful_for.statistical_note: Follow-up time is recorded across three different GDC fields and is null in the most obvious one; derive it from days to death, follow-up records and diagnosis records together, and state your derivation.
